subject: Dedicated GPU pool — Atlas workload projection & pricing framework
messages:
From: Maya Rios <maya@atlasrobotics.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos@atlasrobotics.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas - pilot sizing for Dedicated pool

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Atlas is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. We're moving towards a 12-month committed capacity pilot and I wanted to share high-level workload numbers so you can recommend a pool size and an initial pricing ballpark.

Quick summary of our usage profile (samples attached):
- Peak concurrent users (chat sessions): 220
- Avg requests per user per day: 40 (spiky around business hours)
- Request mix: 65% short prompts (~120 tokens total), 25% medium (~600 tokens), 10% long (~3k tokens)
- Preferred models: mix of 13B and 70B family (we'll try 13B for lower-latency pages, 70B for summarization/batch jobs)
- Target p95 latency: <= 700ms for 13B, <=2s for 70B

Can you and your team propose: 1) recommended GPU pool (type & count) for a committed pool with a 99% availability SLA and burst allowance, 2) suggested monthly committed spend and any discount thresholds for 12-month vs 24-month terms, and 3) what guardrails/operational playbooks you recommend for keeping unit cost low given our model mix?

Attaching a CSV with sampled traffic for an average week.

Best,
Maya
CEO, Atlas Robotics
[attachment: atlas_workload_samples.csv (spreadsheet)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Hi Maya — appreciate the detailed numbers and the file. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Laura (pricing/CS) to give a consolidated recommendation.

Initial notes from my side:
- We can meet your latency goals for 13B at p95 with continuous batching and KV prefix caching on a modest pool; 70B summarization will be more GPU-intensive but can be scheduled to run on reserved capacity with slightly higher latency SLO.
- For committed pricing, we typically offer increasing discounts at commit tiers (monthly equivalent): 50k, 150k, 400k USD. The relative discount for 12 vs 24 months can add ~5-8% depending on the tier and model mix.

Ben — can you take the attached CSV, run a quick sizing calc (tokens/sec, hot-prefix reuse, concurrency), and propose a GPU mix (A100xlarge vs A30-style nodes) plus a draft commit band?

So — will aim to return a single slide with pool sizing and a two-option commercial: 12-month pilot discounted vs 24-month preferred pricing.

Thanks,
Sooyin Lee
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Maya Rios <maya@atlasrobotics.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas - pilot sizing for Dedicated pool

Hi team — I pulled the CSV and ran some quick throughput modeling (attached workbook). Summary up front: recommended production-ready pilot = hybrid pool with 8x A100 80GB equivalent for real-time 70B and higher-concurrency 13B traffic, plus 4x A30-equivalent workers optimized for cost-efficient 13B serving. That maps to roughly ~12 effective GPUs in our runtime (we use heterogeneous task routing).

Sizing rationale (high-level):
- Concurrency: 220 peak concurrent sessions translates to ~1,100 concurrent requests during bursts (avg 5 requests/session in tight windows). Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but we design for 1,100 concurrent request windows.
- Token profile: weighted avg tokens/request ~460; peak tokens/sec during bursts ~500k tokens/sec across the pool.
- Model mix: 70B accounts for 10% of real-time requests but 50% of token volume because of long summaries; we recommend isolating long-summary workloads to dedicated nodes with pre-warming / KV cache enabled.

Recommended operational controls:
1) Keep a small dedicated hot-cache layer (2x A100s) to reduce repeated prefix compute for identical prompt templates.
2) Enable adaptive batching: low-latency traffic uses small batch sizes (8-16), background summarization uses large batches overnight.
3) Set routing policies with model fallbacks (70B -> quantized 70B-8bit or 13B enhanced) for capacity pressure to avoid 503s.

Commercial estimate (ballpark):
- 12-month committed pilot (8 A100e + 4 A30 equiv): $235k/month list -> with tiered commit discount we can offer $188k/month (~20% off) for 12 months.
- 24-month preferred: $235k/month list -> $160k/month (~32% off) with a usage floor guarantee.
- Burst buffer: add 20% headroom for monthly peak (on-demand) billed at reduced overage rate.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_model.xlsx (sizing workbook)

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_capacity_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our ops/finance teams:
1) Can you break the price down into USD per effective GPU-hour equivalent so our finance model can compare to spot/contracted cloud rates?
2) If we do a 12-month pilot with an opt-in for an expanded committed band after month 6, can you guarantee the same per-unit discount for incremental capacity?
3) What SLAs do you commit to for availability and p95 latency, and are credits available for missed SLOs?

Also — what's the recommended on-call/monitoring playbook for the pilot (thinking about runbook link or a short checklist).

Maya

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maya Rios <maya@atlasrobotics.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas - pilot sizing for Dedicated pool

Hi Maya — answering your bullets below and locking in a concrete commercial path: 

1) Unit economics: our commercial math (for the proposed configuration) maps to ~45 USD per effective GPU-hour for the hybrid pool (this normalizes A100-equivalent compute and our runtime optimizations). That includes continuous batching, prefix cache persistence, and kernel-level optimizations; list-equivalent cloud rates would be higher for the same sustained throughput.

2) Expansion guarantee: yes — if Atlas commits to an incremental capacity upgrade within month 6 (i.e., signs an amendment to move from pilot to expanded commit), we will honor the same per-unit discount for the incremental band for the remainder of the contract term. We will include an explicit language clause in the SOW.

3) SLAs & credits: we propose 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool (excludes scheduled maintenance windows) and p95 latency commitments per model class (13B <=700ms, 70B <=2s). Service credits tiered by duration of SLA breach (standard: 5% monthly credit for a single-day breach up to a 25% cap). Details will be in the MSA.

Runbook & ops: attaching our pilot runbook (short checklist + escalation matrix). Key recommendations: on-call rotation (2 engineers), warm-cache maintenance window (daily 05:00-05:30 UTC), automated fallback policy, and monthly capacity health review.

Commercial summary (finalized pilot offer):
- Configuration: Hybrid pool (8x A100e + 4x A30 equiv) 
- Monthly committed fee (12-month): $188,000/month (billed monthly)
- Upfront commitment credit: option for one-time placement fee reduction if pre-paid quarterly
- Burst buffer: 20% on-demand capacity at 50% list overage rate
- Attachments: redwood_dedicated_runbook.pdf and the sizing workbook previously shared

If that works, I'll send a short SOW + amendment that captures expansion guarantee language and SLA terms. Happy to hop on a call to finalize.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Pricing & Customer Success, Redwood Inference
